releaseNotes: Platform release: a founder can now bring someone into a company. Invitations are email-bound and single-use, hashed in the store the way a session token is, and the link is shown to the inviter exactly once — Formation has no mail transport, so it says so plainly and hands over the link rather than pretending to send it. A forwarded link is useless to whoever it was forwarded to: accepting requires being signed in as the invited address. Cancelled, expired, spent, and never-existed are one indistinguishable answer, and guessing is rate limited. The engine's state, reducer, and catalog are untouched; this manifest advances only to keep root package parity.

Membership in the same release: a company always keeps at least one owner — the last owner must promote a successor before stepping down or leaving, which makes ownership transfer a two-step act with no window where the company has nobody who can answer its approvals. Anyone may leave on their own; only an owner removes someone else. Every access change is recorded in the company's own activity rather than a separate log. A closed instance still admits the people it invited: registration accepts an invitation token, which opens the door for that one email address, so turning off open registration no longer silently breaks the invite flow. Schema 4 adds the invitations collection and retires any membership role the capability ladder does not recognise. Checks, 77 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
